text: Refines D-0316 and D-0321 for #604, step 4 of #564's plan: in explicitly configured base checks, a completed Go compiler failure can be a selector's base evidence when a host-owned helper in the prepared toolchain attributes it. The helper validates test-package setup with go list -test, observes a fresh failing go test -c under the captured arguments, compiles production and test dependencies normally, and type-checks the included sources against their real export data, with external tests seeing the package under test with its internal tests' declarations, as go test compiles them. Only a direct use of a missing exported function or composite-literal type, or a missing member of a production-declared type, in the exact top-level pinned test qualifies. Every type error must be such a use in the pinned file and the selected test needs its own, so a neighbor can't borrow it; calls given testing objects, shared helpers, package initializers, children, local bindings, test-only types, a dependency's own copy of the package and unsupported forms are explained refusals. One selection and one compile/failed record carry the full invocation, identity, package, source and execution bindings in TestResult.evidence, and candidates still need fresh authentic runtime passes. Direct discovery, standalone RunAcceptance and trusted evidence keep refusing compiler failures. The review's finding that external tests saw only production's export data was fixed by hand on #606, and the merger ran the real-Docker checks on linux/arm64.
